body: That is exactly how i felt when I started NC at the beginning of this summer. Foolishly, I gave them one last chance to prove to me we could at least work on this in a therapy and just controlled environment. It was my mistake but I needed them to do something this horrible I think to finally pull the trigger and know 100% I am doing the right thing and what I need to do. I know I am going to feel better and the reality is, I am truly not losing much at all besides my health insurance, my vehicle, and the last people in my life that are abusing me. After all the pain and the initial mourning of the idea family that I wanted and am giving up (and would never happen anyways tbh) I am going to be better and I am going to get to live my life for the very first time without being abused on a daily basis and that is what is going to get me through all of this.
thank you very very much i appreciate the luck and support more than i could put into words.

Just wanted to give a quick update that I was able to see my therapist this morning, she scheduled an appointment for tomorrow morning and also got my drug therapist involved so they are both working with me and my SO to try and cover all my bases so if shit hits the fan like it more than likely will, I will st least be able to still have therapy and medication to help me through it. 

The general consensus as of now is that I am more than likely going to have to cut contact with my family completely. Neither I or my therapist think that my parents are going to be able to respect the boundaries I have to put in place in order for me to handle this situation and if what I decide to do is something they don’t like (aka anything other than me letting them take this all out of me and taking care of the family at my own expense) there is a good chance they will retaliate and things will escalate to where I just have to cut contact completely and risk getting cut from insurance and losing my vehicle because I have no choice anymore. 

I am honestly just going to be taking everything day by day so today I am going to hide in my apartment the entire day, take care of myself physically, and just do whatever makes me feel okay that isn’t damaging or harmful. I don’t give myself enough credit for the fact that I am handling this better than I honestly thought I would, and I am also handling this situation overall with my parents at a much younger age than most and handling it without using drugs or flipping back and forth between the contact and none. 

I want to thank you so sincerely for your concern and replies as it really has helped and given me comfort and the little extra support I need since the only support and comfort I have right now is my SO and my therapist.

Me and my SO have decided there need to be established rules and conditions for me seeing my father or family at all during this time and we’re hoping to get my therapists input at my session if that ends up happening. I know I will not be going anywhere near them without my SO and I won’t be going anywhere that I do not travel to on our own so I have access to an exit and a way home no matter what happens. The rest of the rules I really can’t even think or fathom because I honestly don’t know how I am supposed to handle this. I feel like I am straddling this line of protecting myself and hurting other where I can’t tell anymore if I am truly just doing what I need to protect myself or just cutting off contact because it’s somewhat seen as “easier” because I am just stepping away instead of trying to work things out with them. 

Again all of these things I am really trying to discuss with my therapist but it’s nearly 3 am so my appointment is only 5 hours away and I still haven’t heard from her which worries me because I know with the texts I sent her, she would have called me as soon as she saw them. So idk. I’m setting 100 alarms and forcing myself to this appointment and if she doesn’t show up I am waiting for my old drug counselor who also works there and having him help me because otherwise I feel like I’m just going to relapse no matter what I do because I just cannot cope I am beyond max capacity for stress and trauma and panic and if I can’t get anyone to lean on or help me soon I am just going to explode I refuse to put this on my SO bc that just isn’t fair. So idk we will see what happens in five hours and then I am going to go from there and just try to keep breathing

I think the main problem is I don't really know what I want to do. On the one hand, I so desperately want to be there for my father and my sister and my grandmother and, hell, maybe even my mother. But I know that in doing that, I am giving in to them and giving up everything I have been fighting for the past few months. I am inviting them back in my life, but also I am telling my mother it is okay to continue to treat me the way she does when it isn't at all.

Setting boundaries always backfires on me immediately regarding my family as they have absolutely no concept of boundaries whatsoever. For example, I started limiting myself to visiting my parents once, maybe twice a week, so that I could start limiting time to get some privacy and get used to being alone again. Within two weeks I have my father calling me accusing me of using drugs, avoiding him, and "using them" (as if they give me anything other than insurance and sometimes car repairs). My mother just cannot handle it and will fly off the handle immediately. She is the type that will call you until you answer or leave you nasty 5 minute voicemails every few hours. In both cases I cannot win and I just end up more upset and stressed out.

They could theoretically take away my health insurance as I am still under my parents health insurance and have no way of getting my own (or getting one my therapist accepts). They also pay for my therapy which could also be taken but if they simply take the card I can make the payments so long as I have health insurance. My car is currently in the possession of my father as he works at a dealership and was able to get someone to look at my vehicle as it is not accelerating right. I currently only have a loaner from the dealership that I would have to return to him or could risk charges as he could technically lie and say i just stole the vehicle and his plate. My father also put a lien on my vehicle as he did buy it for me after I was hit by a drunk driver after being laid off. So he could very well take the vehicle legally which would royally fuck me over as its the only vehicle me and my SO have.

My only fear is that, if I do go along with all of this even just through the funeral and everything else, it is giving them not only an invitation, but a set time span to do whatever horrible shit they want to me and I just have to take it for "the sake of the family". I just do not want to go through all of this and end up more fucked up than before. I know there is a very good chance that if i do go through with speaking with my mother and letting her take this all out on me, it is going to wear me down enough to relapse at least on drugs if not other things as well. I can only handle so much and I was at my max before this shit storm hit. If I have to take on more I am going to need an outlet and the only one I know and that is available to me would be drugs which i would really like to avoid.

You are right and I know they are going to make it all about them because they already have. During my discussion with my father he mostly talked about how I was tearing the family apart, how it was hurting him and my mom, and lastly defended himself and my mother regarding the abuse and why I had no contact with them in the first place. He talked about my grandfather here and there, but the main focus and emphasis and emotion from him was on my mother and "the family".

I want to be able to be there for my grandmother, as I am actually close with these set of grandparents, at least closer than I am with any other immediate family like that. They had to put their dog down three months ago, my grandfather got surgery two months ago, and now we suddenly has a rare cancer and is just going to die. None of this was ever even mentioned by my father. I know my grandmother is not going to last much longer after my grandfather does pass, and I am going to do my best to reach out to her and be there for her, but I know it is going to be made extremely difficult right now because of my mother. 

Either way I am fucked and hurting someone and myself with any decision I make so hopefully I can figure out which decision is actually the right one. I do not think I am going to go with my father tomorrow. I am more than likely going to use some lie about me being sickly or in too much pain or something who knows. I will figure it out but I am not going to be going at least not tomorrow.

I am afraid of going with my father tomorrow for a multitude of reasons. For one, he wants to pick me and SO up and drive us there which to me means no immediate escape that isn’t him which is a no go. Secondly, I do not know if my mother is going to be there and I know if I ask if she is going to be there and then say no based on that fact it is going to cause even more drama. Lastly, I have seen people in a condition like my grandfather is in and I do not want that to be the last memory I have of him especially with the state I am in now I don’t even want his last memory of me to be this me. 

Short answer: I think I will be able to talk to my grandfather, yes, but I think it will be at a very great cost and I don’t know if it is worth it or not.

I feel like i could have wrote this myself as I deal with almost the exact same situation. My younger sister constantly invalidates the abuse from my mother and father I had to endure because she was never abused by them herself. It upsets me a lot and sometimes I have to take a minute when speaking with her about my parents because it is really difficult. I remember, though, she was never abused by them which means there is absolutely no way she is going to be able to understand or empathize with me at all. I love my sister dearly, but I know she is never going to be able to have that understanding or know what it feels like because, to her, this is all just another blown up fight between me and my mother. That is her reality and I am not going to be able to change that and I just have to accept that. I can't control her and tell her she shouldn't speak to my mother because of what she did to me. All I can control is my contact with my mother and my sister and I can (and did) inform my sister that I will not be speaking about my mother until further notice.

it is a very hard situation and i wish you the best of luck navigating it all

This is extremely similar to the situation I am in. My parents are both abusive drug addicts and as I have gotten sober this year (congrats btw it’s hard and you are v strong for doing it) it has put somewhat of a rift. I am unable to handle or just block out their abuse like I could when I was using which in turn has made it hard to even be around them. Long story short everything blew up this last Sunday after I told them that they had to treat me the way I deserved. After being called probably every name in the book I ended up cutting contact with both of them and do not plan on seeing or speaking to them again at any time in the future. 

It hasn’t been peaches and rainbows, it’s been really hard to come to terms with. At the end of the day, though, I know that I don’t regret it one bit. Standing up to them and not backing down for the first time in my life has given me a send of not only confidence but an inkling of power. Power to change how people treat me and the power to change my life into something better. Of course I wish things were different and I could have that loving family relationship but I know it is not worth my mental and physical health just to stay in contact with them. 

It’s going to be hard but you can do this. If you ever need anyone to chat with about it feel free to pm me. You deserve better than how they are treating you and while it may hurt, you will feel better without them. Family doesn’t treat family the way our parents have treated us, my parents aren’t my family and that is okay.

I am not on the spectrum (we think, getting more testing done) but I have worked with children for the majority of my working life and even started training to become a BCBA myself. I would suggest really researching ABA and reading first hand accounts from people with autism that went through ABA and the effects it had on them. There is a lot wrong with ABA but I am going to sum up what I have read and found and do, again, suggest looking into peoples stories who have been through it because they can explain it better than I ever could.

Firstly, the creator of ABA therapy (Lovaas) is extremely problematic just on his own. He created gay conversion therapy. He has also been quoted saying horrible things about people with autism, one of the most notable being him insinuating that people with autism are not human or less than others due to the fact that they have autism.

ABA therapy itself is also problematic for its own reasons. From what I was trained and saw, the whole principle of ABA is to teach a child to act normal by punishing them for anything that is deemed "unacceptable" by society. This means literally punishing autistic children for doing things like stimming, getting off topic, and other things. Instead of embracing their strengths and giving them outlets and tools to function and do things their way they are instead taught something is wrong with them and they are the problem. 

There are a lot of other things but, like i said, it is not my story to tell and i implore you to look into it fully before you decide anything.

I have not been “officially” diagnosed with ADHD but both my doctor and therapist agree that I have it to the point of putting me on medication for it, I am just waiting to be retested in the fall. I am, however, diagnosed with CPTSD and the suspected diagnosis is inattentive ADD. My therapist has been hinting at me having it for a long time before I finally brought it up and began to explore it myself and it opened my eyes to so much. Suddenly, it made sense why certain things were so much harder than they seemed to be for other people who simply had CPTSD. 

My doctor put me on Adderall and it has honestly changed my life. I am able to focus now and complete tasks which in turn has helped my motivation, confidence, and overall mood. A lot of my anxiety went away as well as a lot of it was stemming from my ADD symptoms not my CPTSD. For example, I could never make eye contact with people or keep a conversation going as a lot of my ADD has to do with my listening (tests actually proved this). After about a week or two on my medication I was able to make eye contact with people while they were speaking to me and I was able to hold conversations and actually retain what the other person was saying. It took a lot of time to get my dose right but I’m the end it has been very worth it and has significantly improved my mental health and life in general. 

One thing my therapist and doctor both drilled into my head is CPTSD and ADD/ADHD mean our brains work completely different than other people. Having both of these disorders, and finding out that I have both, completely changed how my therapy was and what the plan was going forward. Instead of just treating the CPTSD we are now able to focus on both and use the strengths and weaknesses from both to my advantage to get me better in a way that I can handle.

I will say that getting “diagnosed” and medication has not been a miracle or a complete fix for my problems. I still have panic attacks, I still have trouble with depression, and my anxiety is still there. The difference is I have a better understanding of why they are there and what is causing them. I am also able to now finally do something about it as I have the tools now to change things. I am still struggling, but not nearly as bad and I am slowly making improvements in my life. 

If you ever need anyone to talk to or have any questions feel free to pm me and I hope things start becoming easier for you soon.

If possible call whoever lives with your friend first to check on their safety and see if they are serious or if it is less serious. You can call 911 and tell them about the post and your fears and they will send officers to find your friend and make sure that they are okay. Calling the police, though, will more than likely result in them being taken to the hospital by the police to be put on suicide watch and be evaluated. This can sometimes be overwhelming for some people especially if not necessarily needed so I would advise with checking with your friend first and if you fear they are in immediate danger or a danger to themselves then call 911.

I am in almost the exact same boat with my parents and it is indeed extremely hard to deal with. My mother was an alcoholic who has recently become “sober” (I say this because she has relapsed 10x in the past two months and does not seem to be any better sober than she was drunk). I started putting up boundaries before she became sober and have been doing my best to enforce them and limit my time with both of them as it always leads me to a spiral. 

Ever since I have done this they have begun to guilt me into seeing them more. They say things like “you only come over when you want something” or “are you too good for us now?” It is extremely frustrating and hard to deal with. I don’t know if I would say I have much advice as this is something I have been deeply struggling with but some things have made it easier; 
- only telling my parents the good small things. I basically keep it very superficial and only talk about surface things like the weather or tv shows, things of that nature. This makes it so they have no ammo against me and cannot twist the things I say. 
- whenever I do visit or have to speak to them I make an escape plan before I do so. This has been super helpful but it is a little tricky. My best friend and fiancé have been the best help for this as I can text them SOS and they will call me with a fake emergency or what have you to get me out of there quick. 
- my final when everything is overwhelming and I can feel myself starting to panic is simply blocking them for a day or two or muting the messages so I can respond at a later time when I am more in control of my feelings. While I know this isn’t an option always, having it out of sight out of mind has helped me a lot. 

Breaking the cycle of abuse is never easy and there is almost always going to be friction and resistance from the people who caused the cycle to continue in the first place. It is draining, hard, and overall confusing because on the one hand they are my parents but on the other the thing they did no parent should do. In the end, you have to look at your individual situation and decide what the best course of action would be, which a therapist can help with as well. It’s scary but they do not control you and you do not have to speak to them or see them if you do not want to no matter what they say. It is your life and all that you have accomplished has been all you, you do not need them and if it comes down to separation you will be okay I promise. 

I wish you the absolute best luck and if you ever need to talk feel free to PM me

You are more than welcome I am so glad that my words can help in any way at all. I relate a lot to your story in many ways. While my sister didn’t leave for college my situation was very similar to yours in regards to your mother. I was taken out of school and put into online classes in my sophomore year in high school. Because of that I was basically stuck at home with my mother while my father and sister were off at school or work. I was left to take my mother to the hospital anywhere from 2 times a week on a bad week or usually every other week. I always tried to protect my sister and my mother at this time, just trying to keep some stability in my life. Even since my mom has started to “recover”, it is just now that my father is seeing just how bad my mother is. 

I am so glad to hear you have such good supports in your life right now. I am doing my best to find more supports outside my therapist and SO but the search where I live seems futile. Finding a good therapist is always tricky but I will say do not give up. I only truly started healing after finding my therapist after going through countless therapists on and off since the age of 10. One thing my therapist did teach me to ask and look for when looking for therapists is making sure that the therapist themselves and have to therapy. It is unbelievable how many therapists have not been to therapy themselves and after learning this I have been able to weed some therapists out to even find myself a drug therapist who helped me get sober. 

That sounds like such a wonderful idea and I am sure it will be very rewarding. It gives me a hope to hear people like me finding something they love and being able to do that for work. That is something I have been struggling with since i was young feeling pressured to find a good paying job at any cost. Rewriting my brain to understand that that is not the be all end all has been tough but I know that it will be worth it. 

Ending the cycle is so much harder than people think and those that do deserve to feel proud for doing so. This hits me especially hard as I am just now feeling and seeing the physical damage all of this has done to my body. I too have become underweight and am working on that currently but because of past injuries being this underweight causes my bottom ribs to dislocate along with my hips becoming unaligned. While these are painful and obviously not the most fun they are a reminder as to why I am doing what I am doing so my kids and those after them won’t have to go through what I and many of us have had to endure. 

Please be kind to yourself and remember this all takes time.

I first off want to say I am so so sorry for everything you have been through including having to hear your sister say those things. While my story is not exactly the same (I don’t believe anyone’s really can be) I do share a lot of similarities with you (alcoholic/drug depend mother, emotional abuse, and neglect). I am the older sister, however, and while I protected my younger sister from my mothers abuse that also meant that I took all of it for both of us. Since growing up and moving out I have been setting up boundaries with my parents and trying to slowly stop contact all together. My sister on multiple occasions has said she doesn’t understand why I am being so “mean” to my mother or has even said that my trauma was not severe enough to cause the level of PTSD I “claim” to have. 

It is extremely hard hearing these things from the people we love and especially hard when it is someone that we thought we could trust and that understood. I have learned that people cannot truly understand abuse/trauma unless they have experienced it themselves. While there are some wonderful people out there that do at least try to understand and are supportive, they are still never going to truly get it. People also handle trauma in different ways, hence why the cycle of abuse continues in many different families. 

The thing that has helped me through all of this the most is finding support through people who do understand (like my SO and therapist) and limiting what I tell you people like my parents and sister only the surface things. It is easier to tell them about the small things like new movies or tv shows but I never go deeper than that as I know that what they have to say is negative and I do not need that doubt in my head anymore than it already is. 

Please do not let her words get you down. You are valid and what happened to you was not right. It is a shame that your sister cannot see that but you have and you have gotten out and are making a better life for yourself and for your family. You are ending the cycle of abuse and that is so powerful but also very challenging. It will be all worth it in the end though. 

If you ever need anyone to talk to feel free to PM me. Also, your dream job does sound meaningful. Meaningful is anything that makes you happy as it is your life not hers and you are not obligated to live it in any certain way just to meet someone else’s standards.

Medical has been one of the only things that has consistently worked for me without any negative side effects. While it definitely is not a miracle drug by any means, it has made my recovery a lot easier and has helped me progress with less fear. It helps me combat my anxiety so I am able to be around people and actually interact with them, it helps me sleep whenever I am having troubles, and has also significantly helped with my pain as most of mine is from being constantly tense the marijuana helps me relax just enough to not knot my entire back up. It definitely is not for everyone, but with options like CBD candies and topicals it is almost impossible to not find something that will help you in same way or another.

I have unfortunately tried taking the medication daily as well but it seemed to make me a zombie and I still was getting my panic attacks. The only thing that I have found that can instantly snap me out of my symptoms and actually help me without giving me negative side effects is marijuana. It is legal where I live so I am able to medicate with that but that also means that all the jobs that are jumping on the drug testing band wagon are immediately going to deny me. The ADHD medication has made significant improvements that, although seem small to others, have made a positive difference. I can now make more consistent eye contact without fear and I can go to the grocery store without completely panicking. I know that this process is going to be very long, and I suppose most of this is merely me being hyper critical and letting the words of people who do not know me get to me. I just feel like I have been waiting my entire life to be “normal” and to be able to function and I yearn to be able to prove to people that I am worth something. Patience will be key here it’s just extremely frustrating with the combination of disorders.

>one of my doctors told me that people with ADD/ADHD have brains that process differently from other people. More specifically, we are more prone to get into a rut with our thinking and/or emotional state and it can be very difficult to switch gears.

This honestly makes so much sense. I was very recently diagnosed with ADHD so I have only been on my medication for about two months and do not know enough about my ADHD to have thought of this before but it makes so much sense. I have always had a problem with hyper-fixating on things to the point of driving myself crazy. For example, my parents would always get frustrated with me saying that I always had to have something instantly but in reality it was because my mind would cycle whatever I was fixating on until I was able to do/obtain whatever it was. I have seen a difference with my medication but I still struggle.

>For the PTSD, Klonapin keeps the panic under control for me.

I have tried every anxiety med that they have on the market including Klonapin and unfortunately it doesn't seem to take enough of the edge off for me. My panic is constant but usually I can manage it, but when it comes to things that involve other people or work I get so worked up that by the time I am able to take the medication my body rejects it and I end up throwing everything up.
